chunks: And the Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Sayf ibn ʿAmīrah, from Abū Bakr al-Ḥaḍramī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
There is no istinshāq nor maḍmaḍah required upon you, because they are part of the inner cavity.

key_terms.لَيْسَ عَلَيْكَ: Indicates that something is not obligatory upon the legally responsible person.
key_terms.ٱسْتِنْشَاقٌ: Drawing water into the nose during wudu (ablution).
key_terms.ٱلْجَوْفِ: The inner cavity of the body, distinguishing it from the outward parts washed in wudu (ablution).

ai.seo_question: Are istinshāq and maḍmaḍah obligatory in wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning wudu (ablution), stating that istinshāq and maḍmaḍah are not obligatory. The reason given is that the nose and mouth in this context are treated as part of the internal cavity, not the outward limbs required to be washed in wudu (ablution).
